477:                 }

479:         };

483:         if let Some(values) = app.matches.values_of("map-syntax") {
484:             for from_to in values {
485:                 let parts: Vec<_> = from_to.split(':').collect();

487:                 if parts.len() != 2 {
488:                     return Err("Invalid syntax mapping. The format of the -m/--map-syntax option is 'from:to'.".into());

491:                 syntax_mapping.insert(parts[0], parts[1]);

504:                     Some("show-nonprintable")
505:                 } else {
506:                     None
507:                 }
508:             }),

pub struct AppSpec {
    interactive_output: bool,
}

impl AppSpec {
    pub fn from_app(app: &App) -> Self {
        AppSpec {
            interactive_output: app.interactive_output,
        }
    }

    pub fn config<'a>(&self, app: &'a App) -> Result<Config<'a>> {
        let files = app.files();
        let output_components = app.output_components()?;

        let paging_mode = match app.matches.value_of("paging") {
            Some("always") => PagingMode::Always,
            Some("never") => PagingMode::Never,
            Some("auto") | _ => {
                if app.matches.occurrences_of("plain") > 1 {
                    // If we have -pp as an option when in auto mode, the pager should be disabled.
                    PagingMode::Never
                } else if files.contains(&InputFile::StdIn) {
                    // If we are reading from stdin, only enable paging if we write to an
                    // interactive terminal and if we do not *read* from an interactive
                    // terminal.
                    if self.interactive_output && !atty::is(Stream::Stdin) {
                        PagingMode::QuitIfOneScreen
                    } else {
                        PagingMode::Never
                    }
                } else if self.interactive_output {
                    PagingMode::QuitIfOneScreen
                } else {
                    PagingMode::Never
                }
            }
        };

        let mut syntax_mapping = SyntaxMapping::new();

        if let Some(values) = app.matches.values_of("map-syntax") {
            for from_to in values {
                let parts: Vec<_> = from_to.split(':').collect();

                if parts.len() != 2 {
                    return Err("Invalid syntax mapping. The format of the -m/--map-syntax option is 'from:to'.".into());
                }

                syntax_mapping.insert(parts[0], parts[1]);
            }
        }

        let has_decorations = output_components.numbers()
            || output_components.grid()
            || output_components.header()
            || output_components.changes();

        Ok(Config {
            true_color: is_truecolor_terminal(),
            language: app.matches.value_of("language").or_else(|| {
                if app.matches.is_present("show-all") {
                    Some("show-nonprintable")
                } else {
                    None
                }
            }),
            show_nonprintable: app.matches.is_present("show-all"),
            output_wrap: if !self.interactive_output {
                // We don't have the tty width when piping to another program.
                // There's no point in wrapping when this is the case.
                OutputWrap::None
            } else {
                match app.matches.value_of("wrap") {
                    Some("character") => OutputWrap::Character,
                    Some("never") => OutputWrap::None,
                    Some("auto") | _ => {
                        if output_components.plain() && !has_decorations {
                            OutputWrap::None
                        } else if has_decorations {
                            OutputWrap::Character
                        } else {
                            OutputWrap::None
                        }
                    }
                }
            },
            colored_output: match app.matches.value_of("color") {
                Some("always") => true,
                Some("never") => false,
                Some("auto") | _ => self.interactive_output,
            },
            paging_mode,
            term_width: app
                .matches
                .value_of("terminal-width")
                .and_then(|w| {
                    if w.starts_with('+') || w.starts_with('-') {
                        // Treat argument as a delta to the current terminal width
                        w.parse().ok().map(|delta: i16| {
                            let old_width: u16 = Term::stdout().size().1;
                            let new_width: i32 = i32::from(old_width) + i32::from(delta);

                            if new_width <= 0 {
                                old_width as usize
                            } else {
                                new_width as usize
                            }
                        })
                    } else {
                        w.parse().ok()
                    }
                })
                .unwrap_or(Term::stdout().size().1 as usize),
            loop_through: !(self.interactive_output
                || app.matches.value_of("color") == Some("always")
                || app.matches.value_of("decorations") == Some("always")),
            files,
            tab_width: app
                .matches
                .value_of("tabs")
                .map(String::from)
                .or_else(|| env::var("BAT_TABS").ok())
                .and_then(|t| t.parse().ok())
                .unwrap_or(
                    if output_components.plain()
                        && !has_decorations
                        && paging_mode == PagingMode::Never
                    {
                        0
                    } else {
                        4
                    },
                ),
            theme: app
                .matches
                .value_of("theme")
                .map(String::from)
                .or_else(|| env::var("BAT_THEME").ok())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| String::from(BAT_THEME_DEFAULT)),
            line_ranges: {
                let parsed = transpose(
                    app.matches
                        .values_of("line-range")
                        .map(|vs| vs.map(LineRange::from).collect()),
                )?
                .unwrap_or_else(|| vec![]);
                LineRanges::from(
                    parsed
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|range| LineRange {
                            lower: range.lower,
                            upper: range.upper,
                        })
                        .collect(),
                )
            },
            output_components,
            syntax_mapping,
            pager: app.matches.value_of("pager"),
            use_italic_text: match app.matches.value_of("italic-text") {
                Some("always") => true,
                _ => false,
            },
            highlight_lines: app
                .matches
                .values_of("highlight-line")
                .and_then(|ws| ws.map(|w| w.parse().ok()).collect())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
        })
    }
}

The fix is complete and validated. Summary of changes:

**`src/clap_app.rs`** — Removed the `cache` subcommand (and the `InferSubcommands` prefix-matching problem, plus the `Path::new("cache").exists()` workaround) and replaced it with hidden top-level flags: `--cache-build`, `--cache-clear`, `--cache-source`, `--cache-target`, `--cache-blank`, with `requires("cache-build")` validation on the secondary flags.

**`src/app.rs`** (src/app.rs:108) — Config-file parsing is now skipped when any argument starts with `--cache` instead of when the first arg equals `cache`.

**`src/main.rs`** — `run()` handles `cache-build`/`cache-clear` flags via `run_cache_subcommand` instead of the subcommand match arm; the special "print file named cache" fallback was removed since `bat cache` is now just an ordinary file argument.

Docs (`README.md`, `assets/README.md`, `doc/README-ja.md`) updated to use `bat --cache-build` / `bat --cache-clear`.

- `can_print_file_named_cache` and `does_not_print_unwanted_file_named_cache` (the FAIL_TO_PASS cases) pass
- All 34 integration tests pass
